facts.title: Country and period
facts.text: Country: Rwanda (RWA). Annual period 2014–2025, monthly series 2014-01-01 → 2025-10-01. Levels: ADM1, ADM2. Synthetic data: no.

facts.title: National trend
facts.text: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in Rwanda changed by +16.3% per year (95% CI: +12.9% to +20.0%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is +6.6% relative to the previous 12 months. (confidence high: significant trend (p < 0.01; n = 12))

facts.title: Regions
facts.text: Of 30 ADM2 units, 30 show significant growth, 0 are stagnating and 0 are declining. Light remains concentrated: City of Kigali accounts for 47% of national light. (confidence medium: classification of 30 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10)

facts.title: Convergence
facts.text: Across ADM2 units, light per capita converges: the least-lit units are catching up. (confidence medium: β = −0.055 [−0.069; −0.042], n = 30)

facts.title: Link with GDP
facts.text: The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 2.38 in levels (95% CI: 2.12 to 2.64, R² = 0.96, 12 years) and −0.37 in growth rates (CI: −1.36 to 0.63). Out of sample, light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of 0.28 (mean absolute error: 3.6 percentage points of growth). (confidence medium: clear relationship but only 12 years)

facts.title: Shocks
facts.text: The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of +4.7% (05/2021), return to the pre-shock level after 15 months. (confidence low: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability)

facts.title: Inequality and access
facts.text: The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.50 in 2025 (significant decrease since 2014). About 0.31 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (54% of the inhabited population). (confidence medium: sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.31 to 0.37 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection)

facts.title: Industrial zones
facts.text: 22 industrial clusters detected from concordant satellite signals: 6 heavy industry, 0 business parks & logistics, 1 oil & gas sites and 15 isolated sites to verify. They emit 13.7% of national light (latest year); their light changes by +14.9% per year. City of Kigali has the most industrial activity. (confidence low: precision 32% and recall 26% against the reference list)

facts.title: Summer tourism
facts.text: 8 of 30 units show a net summer light excess of at least 10%: Nyarugenge (City of Kigali), Nyamagabe (Southern Province), Gasabo (City of Kigali), Gicumbi (Northern Province). The median net excess reaches +24% in the most touristic zone. The season index (base 100 = 2019) falls to nan in 2020 and stands at nan in 2025. (confidence low: no hotel-night statistics to validate the indicator)

facts.title: Urbanisation
facts.text: The lit area changes by +21.3% per year, against +2.4% for population. Of 30 ADM2 units: 30 show electrified urbanisation, 0 balanced growth, 0 unlit growth. Between 2014 and 2025, 3,133 km² became lit, of which 1,281 km² in already inhabited areas (≈ 111k newly lit inhabitants). Largest expansion: Bugesera (Eastern Province), Nyagatare (Eastern Province), Rwamagana (Eastern Province). (confidence medium: rank correlation of 0.42 with GHSL built-up growth (30 units))

facts.title: Key indicators
facts.text: Annual growth of light = +16.3% (2014–2025, robust slope (Theil–Sen)); Last 12 months vs previous 12 = +6.6% (seasonally adjusted series, up to 10/2025); Light–GDP elasticity = 2.38 (95% CI 2.12 to 2.64 · confidence medium); Gini of light per capita = 0.50 (ADM2 units, 2025); People in the dark = 0.31 M (54% of the inhabited population, 2025); Share of the top region = 47% (City of Kigali, 2025); Industrial clusters = 22 (14% of national light); Tourist zones = 8 (max. summer excess +24% (Nyarugenge (City of Kigali))); Lit area = +21.3% (annual growth; population +2.4%/yr)

facts.title: Recommendations
facts.text: • Use night-time lights as a leading and subnational indicator, as a complement to — never a replacement for — the national accounts. • Publish regional GDP estimates as experimental statistics, with intervals and a methodological note, after comparison with available regional accounts. • Cross-check the map of populations “in the dark” against grid-connection registers: the average gap with the World Bank access rate is -12 percentage points. • Document breaks detected without an associated event (sensor change, outage, local event) before any economic interpretation. • Have the 15 isolated sites checked on high-resolution imagery and complete the official register of industrial zones used as the validation reference. • Monitor the light of industrial clusters monthly as a leading indicator of industrial output, and compare it with the industrial production index where one exists. • Publish the tourist season index right after the summer (VIIRS data are available within weeks), ahead of hotel-night statistics, and recalibrate it on them every year. • Cross newly lit areas with urban plans and grid-connection registers to tell planned expansion, informal settlements and rural electrification apart. • Update the dashboard every quarter (monthly VIIRS series) and every year (annual VNL composites).

facts.title: Limitation: What lights measure
facts.text: Upward radiance emitted around 01:30: agriculture, daytime trade, poorly lit services and the rural informal economy are poorly captured.

facts.title: Limitation: Saturation and blooming
facts.text: DMSP saturates in city centres (DN 63) and “blooms” beyond lit areas; VIIRS is much better, but blooming still inflates the lit area of cities.

facts.title: Limitation: Gas flares and isolated sites
facts.text: The automatic mask may remove isolated mines, ports or power plants, and miss small flares; candidates are exported for verification.

facts.title: Limitation: Clouds, seasons, moon
facts.text: Cloudy months are only partially observed; STL removes average seasonality but not an abnormal season (snow, late monsoon).

facts.title: Limitation: Product breaks
facts.text: DMSP and VIIRS are not directly comparable: the harmonised long series (Li et al., 2020) is a modelled product, to be read for trends only.

facts.title: Limitation: NTL–GDP elasticity
facts.text: Estimated on 10 to 30 annual observations: wide intervals, possible instability, a non-causal relationship that varies with the level of development.

facts.title: Limitation: Access to electricity
facts.text: “Inhabited without light” ≠ “not connected”: a connected household with low consumption is invisible; the indicator depends strongly on the radiance threshold and the population data.

facts.title: Limitation: Administrative boundaries
facts.text: geoBoundaries/GAUL may differ from official boundaries; small ADM2 units are sensitive to light spilling over from neighbouring units.

facts.title: Limitation: Industrial zones
facts.text: Detection relies on thresholds: a power plant, a port or a large shopping centre can meet the signals; a dimly lit factory without visible emissions is missed. Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) are coarser than VIIRS: NO₂/SO₂/heat signals describe a neighbourhood, not a building.

facts.title: Limitation: Summer tourism
facts.text: The summer excess captures any rise in summer light (second homes, diaspora visits, festivals, construction), not only tourism; at high latitudes, very short summer nights reduce VIIRS observations. Ramadan changes night-time activity: the summers concerned are flagged.

facts.title: Limitation: Urbanisation
facts.text: The lit area depends on the detection threshold and on light blooming around cities; a connected but dimly lit neighbourhood stays invisible. Population (GHSL/WorldPop) is modelled from censuses: its growth is not an independent observation, and years between two epochs are interpolated.

facts.title: City of Kigali (ADM1)
facts.text: City of Kigali (ADM1, 2025): share of national light 47.3%, annual growth +13.2% (CI +10.5% to +15.6%, class Growth), light per capita 0.271, population 0.09 M, in the dark 3%, estimated GDP (experimental) 7.70 bn USD.

facts.title: Eastern Province (ADM1)
facts.text: Eastern Province (ADM1, 2025): share of national light 21.9%, annual growth +29.4% (CI +26.5% to +34.6%, class Growth), light per capita 0.054, population 0.20 M, in the dark 62%, estimated GDP (experimental) 3.56 bn USD.

facts.title: Southern Province (ADM1)
facts.text: Southern Province (ADM1, 2025): share of national light 12.7%, annual growth +15.0% (CI +11.7% to +19.7%, class Growth), light per capita 0.041, population 0.16 M, in the dark 65%, estimated GDP (experimental) 2.07 bn USD.

facts.title: Western Province (ADM1)
facts.text: Western Province (ADM1, 2025): share of national light 10.8%, annual growth +16.5% (CI +11.4% to +20.1%, class Growth), light per capita 0.038, population 0.14 M, in the dark 60%, estimated GDP (experimental) 1.76 bn USD.

facts.title: Northern Province (ADM1)
facts.text: Northern Province (ADM1, 2025): share of national light 7.2%, annual growth +21.8% (CI +13.9% to +26.2%, class Growth), light per capita 0.041, population 0.09 M, in the dark 62%, estimated GDP (experimental) 1.16 bn USD.

facts.title: ADM2: ranking
facts.text: 30 ADM2 units. Classes: Growth 30. Fastest growth: Kirehe (Eastern Province) (+41.6%), Bugesera (Eastern Province) (+40.3%), Burera (Northern Province) (+39.0%), Rulindo (Northern Province) (+34.8%), Nyagatare (Eastern Province) (+32.0%), Gakenke (Northern Province) (+31.4%), Kamonyi (Southern Province) (+31.2%), Rutsiro (Western Province) (+31.2%). Slowest: Karongi (Western Province) (+7.6%), Nyamagabe (Southern Province) (+9.5%), Ruhango (Southern Province) (+9.7%), Nyarugenge (City of Kigali) (+9.8%), Gicumbi (Northern Province) (+11.4%), Nyanza (Southern Province) (+12.4%), Huye (Southern Province) (+12.6%), Gasabo (City of Kigali) (+12.6%).

facts.title: ADM2: brightest
facts.text: Brightest units: Gasabo (City of Kigali) (23.6%), Kicukiro (City of Kigali) (16.5%), Bugesera (Eastern Province) (8.0%), Nyarugenge (City of Kigali) (7.1%), Rwamagana (Eastern Province) (4.4%), Rubavu (Western Province) (3.5%), Nyagatare (Eastern Province) (3.5%), Musanze (Northern Province) (3.1%), Kamonyi (Southern Province) (2.8%), Rusizi (Western Province) (2.8%).

facts.title: Convergence and concentration
facts.text: β-convergence (ADM2): β = -0.055 (CI -0.069 to -0.042, n = 30). β < 0 with a fully negative CI = convergence. Share of the leading region: 66.1% in 2014 → 47.3% in 2025; HHI 0.305.

facts.title: Elasticity (levels)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in levels: β = 2.38 (95% CI 2.12 to 2.64, R² = 0.96, n = 12, confidence medium: clear relationship but only 12 years). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (growth rates)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in growth rates: β = -0.37 (95% CI -1.36 to 0.63, R² = 0.01, n = 11, confidence low: n = 11, not significant (p = 0.47)). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (long DMSP–VIIRS series)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in long DMSP–VIIRS series: β = 1.04 (95% CI 0.73 to 1.35, R² = 0.93, n = 30, confidence high: n = 30, p < 0.01, narrow CI). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Out-of-sample tracking
facts.text: Out of sample, light-based growth has a correlation of 0.28 with official growth; mean absolute error 3.6 percentage point.

facts.title: Shock: COVID-19
facts.text: COVID-19 (2020-03-01 → 2021-06-30): trough of 4.7% on 2021-05-01, back to the pre-shock level after 15 months. Distinguishable from noise: no.

facts.title: Regional impact of shocks
facts.text: Hardest-hit regions (trough): City of Kigali -20.5 % (covid19), Northern Province -5.6 % (covid19), Eastern Province 10.3 % (covid19), Southern Province 16.2 % (covid19), Western Province 21.0 % (covid19).

facts.title: Gini and Theil
facts.text: Gini of light per capita (ADM2): 0.672 in 2014 → 0.503 in 2025 (change -0.169, bootstrap CI -0.231 to -0.058). Theil T 0.462; between-region share 77%.

facts.title: Population in the dark
facts.text: People in inhabited areas without detectable light: 0.34 M (79%) in 2014 → 0.31 M (54%) in 2025. Urban/rural light-per-capita ratio 0.7. Proxy of electricity access, sensitive to the threshold.

facts.title: Comparison with the World Bank
facts.text: Average gap between the share of people in lit areas and the World Bank electricity-access rate: -12.0 points.

facts.title: Industrial zones: summary
facts.text: 22 industrial clusters (≥ 3 of 6 signals): Isolated site to verify 15, Heavy industry 6, Oil, gas & flares 1. Share of national light: 13.7%; annual growth +14.9%. Validation (OpenStreetMap): precision 32%, recall 26%.

facts.title: Main industrial clusters
facts.text: IND-001 — Isolated site to verify in Gasabo (City of Kigali) (72.025 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-002 — Heavy industry in Musanze (Northern Province) (11.825 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-006 — Isolated site to verify in Nyarugenge (City of Kigali) (4.515 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-003 — Heavy industry in Rubavu (Western Province) (10.105 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-004 — Heavy industry in Rusizi (Western Province) (9.245 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-005 — Isolated site to verify in Nyagatare (Eastern Province) (6.45 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-007 — Isolated site to verify in Rwamagana (Eastern Province) (4.3 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-008 — Isolated site to verify in Bugesera (Eastern Province) (3.225 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-009 — Isolated site to verify in Bugesera (Eastern Province) (2.15 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-010 — Isolated site to verify in Gatsibo (Eastern Province) (1.505 km², 3 signals, confidence low)

facts.title: Industry — City of Kigali
facts.text: City of Kigali: 2 industrial cluster(s), 76.5 km², 18.4% of the region's light.

facts.title: Industry — Eastern Province
facts.text: Eastern Province: 13 industrial cluster(s), 24.7 km², 8.8% of the region's light.

facts.title: Industry — Western Province
facts.text: Western Province: 4 industrial cluster(s), 21.1 km², 16.6% of the region's light.

facts.title: Industry — Northern Province
facts.text: Northern Province: 2 industrial cluster(s), 12.5 km², 16.9% of the region's light.

facts.title: Industry — Southern Province
facts.text: Southern Province: 1 industrial cluster(s), 0.6 km², 0.3% of the region's light.

facts.title: Industrial light and value added
facts.text: Correlation between the growth of industrial light and of industry value added (World Bank, NV.IND.TOTL.KD): -0.03 over 11 years.

facts.title: Tourism: tourist zones
facts.text: 8 tourist zone(s) out of 30 ADM2 units (net summer excess ≥ 10%, peak months [12, 1]): Nyarugenge (City of Kigali) (+24%, confidence high), Nyamagabe (Southern Province) (+18%, confidence medium), Gasabo (City of Kigali) (+16%, confidence high), Gicumbi (Northern Province) (+15%, confidence medium), Kicukiro (City of Kigali) (+14%, confidence medium), Musanze (Northern Province) (+11%, confidence high), Kamonyi (Southern Province) (+11%, confidence medium), Rubavu (Western Province) (+10%, confidence medium).

facts.title: Tourist season index
facts.text: Season index (base 100 = 2019): . Years when Ramadan overlaps the season: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025.

facts.title: Urbanisation: lit area and population
facts.text: National lit area: +21.3% per year; population: +2.4% per year. Classes (ADM2): Electrified urbanisation 30.

facts.title: Urbanisation: newly lit areas
facts.text: Between 2014 and 2025: 3,133 km² newly lit, of which 1,281 km² already inhabited (electrification, ≈ 111k people) and 1,852 km² of new settlements; 6 km² lost their light.

facts.title: Urbanisation: units
facts.text: Fastest lit-area expansion: Burera (Northern Province) (+54.9%/yr), Kirehe (Eastern Province) (+53.3%/yr), Rutsiro (Western Province) (+44.7%/yr), Bugesera (Eastern Province) (+40.9%/yr), Gakenke (Northern Province) (+40.2%/yr), Rulindo (Northern Province) (+38.6%/yr). Unlit growth (population faster than light): none.

facts.title: Validation with GHSL built-up
facts.text: Spearman rank correlation between lit-area growth and GHSL built-up growth: 0.42 (p = 0.020, 30 units).

facts.title: Quality and international standards
facts.text: Night-time-light indicators are experimental statistics: they complement official statistics and do not replace them. Every output is published with its method, validation, uncertainty, limitations and a confidence level. Frameworks applied: UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics, DQAF, UNECE GSBPM, FAIR principles.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Time dynamics
facts.text: Validation: Trend significance (Mann–Kendall) and monthly/annual consistency (p-value = < 0.0001). Uncertainty: 95% CI of annual growth: +12.9% to +20.0% Limitations: Cloud cover and short summer nights; light is not value added. Status: experimental statistic; confidence high.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Regional growth and convergence
facts.text: Validation: Rank correlation with tropospheric NO₂ (independent source) (Spearman ρ = 0.56). Uncertainty: Class assigned only if |slope| ≥ threshold and p < α; CI of β (robust errors). Limitations: Small units: noise and light blooming between neighbours. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Light–GDP relationship
facts.text: Validation: Out-of-sample tracking of official growth (correlation / MAE (pp) = 0.28 / 3.6). Uncertainty: 95% CI of the elasticity: 2.12 to 2.64; 80% and 95% prediction intervals. Limitations: Short annual sample; regional GDP is an experimental statistic to be checked against regional accounts. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Shocks and resilience
facts.text: Validation: Does the trough exceed ordinary variability? (trough (main shock) = 4.7% — no). Uncertainty: Pre-shock month-to-month variability (robust SD); unexplained breaks flagged. Limitations: Shocks hitting poorly lit activities (agriculture, daytime services) are underestimated. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Inequality and electrification
facts.text: Validation: Gap with the World Bank electricity-access rate (mean gap (pp) = -12.0). Uncertainty: Range across radiance thresholds; bootstrap CI of the Gini. Limitations: Proxy of outdoor lighting, not of connection: a connected but dimly lit household looks “in the dark”. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Industrial zones
facts.text: Validation: Comparison with the reference list (OpenStreetMap) (precision / recall / F1 = 32% / 26% / 0.28). Uncertainty: Per-cluster confidence from the number of strong signals; isolated sites to verify. Limitations: Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) resolution: signals describe a neighbourhood. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Seasonal tourism
facts.text: Validation: Correlation with hotel nights (r = not available). Uncertainty: p-value per unit; 2020–2021 excluded from the classification. Limitations: Any summer activity (diaspora, second homes, festivals) is captured, not only tourism. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Urbanisation signals
facts.text: Validation: Rank correlation with GHSL built-up area growth (independent source) (Spearman ρ = 0.42). Uncertainty: Persistence required over two years to limit noise; ± 1 pp margin between growth rates before classifying. Limitations: Light measures outdoor lighting, not urbanisation in the administrative sense; blooming widens cities; GHSL population is interpolated between epochs. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Method — Method
facts.text: Data: VIIRS DNB monthly (VCMSLCFG) and annual VNL V2, harmonised DMSP–VIIRS, daily Black Marble, GHSL/WorldPop, Sentinel-5P NO₂/SO₂, MODIS LST, World Bank. Cleaning: pixels valid if cf_cvg ≥ 2, unit-month kept if ≥ 80% of pixels observed, spikes replaced, background and gas flares masked.

facts.title: Method — Dynamics
facts.text: Dynamics: robust STL on log(sum of lights), Theil–Sen trend + Mann–Kendall test, year-on-year growth, breaks by piecewise-linear segmentation with a BIC penalty.

facts.title: Method — Regions
facts.text: Regions: robust growth per unit, Growth/Decline class if |slope| ≥ 1%/yr and p < 0.10; β-convergence (robust OLS), σ-convergence, Herfindahl index.

facts.title: Method — GDP
facts.text: GDP: log(NTL) = α + β log(GDP) in levels and growth rates, HAC standard errors, DW/BP/JB diagnostics, out-of-sample tracking; experimental regional GDP allocated by light (γ = 1 and 0.5).

facts.title: Method — Shocks
facts.text: Shocks: trough = largest gap to the 12-month pre-shock level of the seasonally adjusted series, recovery = return to that level; daily Black Marble index (7-day rolling median).

facts.title: Method — Inequality
facts.text: Inequality: population-weighted Gini, Theil (between/within decomposition) and Lorenz; population in the dark = residents of pixels ≥ 5 people below 0.5 nW (sensitivity 0.25/0.5/1).

facts.title: Method — Industry
facts.text: Industry: six signals per pixel (light ≥ 5 nW, light per resident, GHSL non-residential built-up, Sentinel-5P NO₂ and SO₂, MODIS surface heat); pixels with ≥ 3 signals grouped into clusters; typology, confidence from concordant signals, precision/recall validation (official list or OSM).

facts.title: Method — Tourism
facts.text: Tourism: summer excess = log(peak-month light / shoulder-month light); net of the median of comparable units at the same latitude; tourist zone if ≥ +10% and significant over ≥ 3 summers; season index base 100; Ramadan flagged; validation with hotel nights.

facts.title: Method — Urbanisation
facts.text: Urbanisation: annual lit area (pixels ≥ threshold) and its growth (Theil–Sen) compared with population growth (GHSL/WorldPop); newly lit areas (dark in the first 2 years, lit in the last 2), split into electrification of already inhabited areas and new settlements; validation with GHSL BUILT-S built-up growth.

tools.name: search_facts
tools.description: Search the published facts (key messages, methods, limitations, national figures) for those answering a question. Use it first for any general question.

tools.name: rank_units
tools.description: Rank regions (ADM1) or districts (ADM2) by an indicator for the latest year: fastest growth, largest share of population in the dark, etc.

tools.name: unit_profile
tools.description: Full profile of a region or district: latest indicators, light trend, growth class, industrial and tourist zones.

tools.name: compare_units
tools.description: Compare several units (or the country) on an annual indicator between two years: levels, change and compound annual growth rate.

tools.name: make_chart
tools.description: Draw a chart (annual series of an indicator for units, or a ranking bar chart) shown in the conversation.

tools.name: map_action
tools.description: Drive the dashboard's interactive map: show a year, compare two years (swipe), focus on a unit, or show a layer (lights, population in the dark, indicator, industrial clusters, tourist zones).
